title: The first refuge was Africa
hookLine: the first Muslim refugees were welcomed in Abyssinia

lines: ASMA TAKES IT TO THE PROPHET.
cards: Umar ibn al-Khattab walks into his daughter Hafsah's house in Medina and finds a visitor, a woman just back from across the sea: Asma bint Umays.
When he learns where she has been, he tells her: we emigrated before you did, so we have more right to the Messenger of Allah than you. Asma doesn't laugh. She's angry.
She says she won't eat or drink until she has taken it to the Prophet ﷺ himself. Where had she been? Today: the first refuge was Africa.

teach.b: Asma had been in Abyssinia, across the Red Sea in East Africa. Years earlier, in Mecca, believers who were being persecuted had crossed that sea, and a Christian king, the Negus, had sheltered them.
Asma and her husband Ja'far were among them. Before there was a Medina to go to, there was Africa. Here's what she says back to Umar, as Sahih al-Bukhari reports it, in paraphrase.
You were with the Prophet. He fed your hungry and taught your ignorant.

teach.h: WE WERE FAR AWAY, AMONG STRANGERS.
teach.b: We were far away, among strangers, in a land where we were hated, all of it for the sake of Allah and His Messenger. So she goes to the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and tells him what Umar said.
And he answers: Umar has no more right to me than you do.
He and his companions made one hijrah. You, the people of the ship, made two. One across the sea to Africa, and one from Africa to Medina.
The Prophet counts the African years as a hijrah in their own right, not a detour. And the report adds one more detail.

teach.h: THEY CAME TO HEAR HER TELL IT.
teach.b: Abu Musa, who sailed home with them, says the people of the ship came to Asma in groups to hear her tell it, and nothing in the world made them happier or meant more to them than what the Prophet had said.
That's where the story of Islam in Africa begins: not with an army, but with refugees and a king who would not hand them over.

how: Muslims tell the emigration to Abyssinia as the first hijrah, and the Negus's protection of the refugees is remembered in sermons and lessons about sheltering the persecuted.

games.why: she took it to the Prophet, who said the people of the ship had made two hijrahs, and Umar's group one.

practice: Bring to mind a place or a person that sheltered you when you needed it: a grandparent's house, a friend's sofa, a teacher's classroom at lunch, a country that took your family in.
Let it come clearly, the door, the smell, the face, and let yourself be grateful. If you pray, ask Allah to reward that person or place; if not, simply say thank you in your head, and mean it.

wordCard.voice: Hijrah. Emigration for the sake of Allah, like the one believers fleeing Mecca made to Abyssinia, the first refuge, before Medina. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: emigration, leaving one place for another for the sake of Allah.

carryVoice: Your line: africa sheltered them first. Two hijrahs, and both counted. That's day nine hundred sixty-five.
